heroSubtitle: Organize documents and structured knowledge, ask grounded questions, and turn evidence into clear analysis briefings — one platform for your team's knowledge work.
painDesc: We built openKMS because teams struggle with:
pain1Text: Documents, PDFs, and notes live in silos—email, shared drives, wikis—making it hard to find what you need.
pain2Title: Evidence can't travel with the story
pain2Text: Tables, domain facts, and document citations sit in different tools, so briefings lose the trail back to source.
pain3Title: Manual work that should be automated
pain3Text: Repetitive document parsing, layout extraction, and indexing drain time and introduce errors.
ben1Text: Organize documents, articles, and wikis in channel trees. Upload PDF and images—AI parses them into searchable Markdown.
ben2Text: Build knowledge bases you can ask. Explore object types, links, and datasets so analysis starts from facts—not guesses.
ben3Text: Agents can pull evidence across content and data, then produce multi-slide analysis presentations stakeholders can open and navigate.
funcKb2: Semantic search over chunks and FAQs (pgvector when configured)
funcOnt1: Datasets mapped from PostgreSQL data sources
funcOnt2: Object types and link types for your domain model
funcOnt3: Optional Neo4j indexing and graph exploration
funcAgent1: Installable skill for external coding agents
funcAgent2: Research across documents, knowledge bases, and ontology data
funcAgent3: Ship interactive multi-slide analysis presentations from evidence
funcPipe1: Configurable document pipelines and command templates
funcPipe2: Async parsing runs; per-channel pipeline and auto-process
funcPipe3: Models linked to pipelines for OCR / VL / extraction
ctaReady: Ready to put evidence behind every briefing?
